items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are mostly clear (useRestoredData, useRestoredError), but none of the new public exports have docs (createPersisterRestoreResult, reconcileQueryState). types.ts adds `import type { PersisterRestoreResult }` in the middle of the file. A useful 'We must resolve the promise here' comment was deleted.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Query.fetch applies the restore with `this.setState(newState)` rather than a dedicated reducer action. A full default QueryState literal is copied into both query.ts and createPersister.ts. The afterRestoreMacroTask setState is kept even though it is now redundant. On the plus side, single and bulk restore share reconcileQueryState.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Persisted counts and timestamps are not normalised; missing fields fall back via `?? current`. The fallback state stamps `dataUpdatedAt: Date.now()`. Public types use `PersisterRestoreResult<T, any>`. Status is forced to 'error' whenever an error exists, ignoring the persisted status. No errors are swallowed.

items.name: Restore path API contract
items.name_zh: 恢复路径 API 约定
items.evidence: The helper is exported from query-core and marked with a Symbol brand, and the restore path skips onSuccess/onSettled with fetchStatus idle. The state is applied via setState, not a dedicated action. Bulk restore reuses reconcileQueryState but calls setState/build itself. The signature makes data and state optional (`data?: TData; state?:`).

items.name: Existing persister contract preserved
items.name_zh: 保持既有 persister 约定
items.evidence: The plain-data path in Query.fetch is untouched, and the new exports and the widened QueryPersister type are additive. Internally, persisterFn now returns a restore marker instead of data, and restoreQueries switched from setQueryData to reconcile/build. Those behaviour shifts are only partly covered by tests.
